What we buy

We're picky,
in a good way.

We pay cash for what we can resell, and donate the rest. We don't have set rates, but we have a structure for how we assess it.

↩
Why it's free: Reselling quality clothing is what funds the whole operation — drop-off and CBD & East Auckland pickup alike. No fees, no catches — the resale value covers it.
The three grades

Every item gets sorted on the spot.

We make one overall grade decision for your collection — you'll know exactly what you're getting before we take anything.

Premium grade
Valuable & resellable clothing
Paid individually
assessed piece by piece
Reserved for pieces with real resale value — brands people actually seek out, condition that holds up, styles that move. These are assessed one by one, not lumped together. Men's pieces are especially sought after right now.
What qualifies
Vintage Levi's, Wrangler, Lee denim Surf & skate — Billabong, Quiksilver, Volcom, Ripcurl Outdoor & workwear — Carhartt, Patagonia, Arc'teryx Designer labels in good condition Rugby jerseys, band tees, graphic tees with character Quality men's shirts, jackets, trousers
Tip: flag any standout pieces when you book — we'll look out for them.
Standard grade
General adult clothing
Paid per kg
whole collection, one price
Most collections fall here. Wearable adult clothing in mixed condition — no standout pieces, but clean and sellable. We weigh the lot and pay a flat rate per kilogram. Simple, fast, no haggling.
What qualifies
Everyday adult men's and women's clothing Good condition, no major damage Mixed labels and styles Tops, bottoms, dresses, knitwear Coats and jackets without brand premium
A typical wardrobe clear-out — 3 bags of mixed adult clothing — usually lands here.
Donation grade
Worn, damaged, or low-value items
Donated free
to local charities · nothing to landfill
Anything we can't resell goes to local charities and op shops — including Dove Hospice, Pregnancy Choice, Red Cross, and the Salvation Army. We don't charge for this — it's part of the deal. Nothing gets thrown out.
What goes here
Children's and kids' clothing (all of it) Adult clothing with heavy wear or damage Low-value or unbranded items we can't resell Clothing mixed into a premium or standard lot
You don't need to sort anything before we arrive — we handle the grading on the day.
What's outside our scope

Mostly clothing. A few exceptions.

We focus on adult clothing — that's where we can do our job properly. Everything below is generally outside our scope.

Shoes — occasionally
We're not primarily a footwear buyer, but if you've got a standout pair alongside a good clothing collection, mention it when you get in touch and we'll take a look.
No bags or accessories
Handbags, backpacks, belts, hats, scarves — not accepted. Clothing (and the occasional shoe) is where we stay focused.
No homewares or linen
Bedding, towels, curtains, cushions — none of it. We're a clothing service, not a general op shop collection.
No toys, books, or electronics
If it's not a piece of clothing, we can't take it. Kids' clothes are fine (donated) — everything else isn't.
Got a mix? That's fine — just bag your clothing separately and leave the rest. You don't need to sort clothing into grades; we do that. Just keep non-clothing items out of the bags.
On the day

How the assessment works.

01
We look through everything
We go through your bags there and then, pulling out anything that looks premium. This takes 5–15 minutes depending on the volume.
02
We make you an offer
Premium pieces get individual prices. The rest gets weighed. We give you a total and you decide — no pressure, no obligation to accept.
03
Paid before we leave
If you're happy, we pay via bank transfer on the spot. Everything we take goes with us — nothing gets left behind to sort later.

"We're a resale business — and we're upfront about that. Great clothing deserves a second life, not a landfill."
